sentences.text: Court No. - 11 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC ANTICIPATORY BAIL APPLICATION U/S 438 CR.P.C. No. - 503 of 2022 Applicant :- Vartika Singh Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And Another Counsel for Applicant :- Rohit Kumar Tripathi,Anuja Bajpai Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. has been filed for anticipatory bail in F.I.R.
No.402/2020 under sections 509/419/420/467/468/471/120-B/34 I.P.C., R/W 66/67 (C) IT Act 2008 Police Station Musafirkhana, District Amethi.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant is falsely implicated in the present case.

He further submitted that the F.I.R. in question was challenged in Writ Petition No.1383 of 2021 (MB), in which, the stay order was passed on 19.01.2021 and during the course of investigation, applicant was not taken into custody and charge-sheet was filed by the Investigating Officer in the most mechanical manner.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the investigation was conducted without considering the evidences provided by the applicant and without sending the alleged documents to F.S.L. for expert opinion.

He further submitted that the applicant cooperated in the investigation,

therefore, the applicant is entitled to get anticipatory bail.

sentences.text:
Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer of applicant and submitted that after detailed investigation,
sufficient evidence has been collected by the Investigating Officer, thereafter, the charge sheet has been filed but he does not dispute on the judicial orders passed in favour of the applicant and he also conceded the fact that the alleged documents were not sent to F.S.L. for expert opinion.
Considering the argument of learned counsel for the parties and going through the contents of the FIR, counter affidavit, as well as other relevant documents, and the order passed by Writ Court,
order passed by Hon'ble Apex Court
, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled for anticipatory bail.
In view of the above, the application is disposed of.

In case, the applicant, namely, Vartika Singh is taken into custody, she shall be released by the Station House Officer of the police station concerned, on her furnishing personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties of each of like amount with the following condition:-
(i) The applicant shall not commit or participate in any offence similar to the offence of which she is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which she is suspected.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that she shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed,
either personally or through her counsel.
In case of her absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against her under Section 229-A IPC.

(v) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure her presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against her, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against her in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
